clue.text: A jogger's complaint?

parts.note: a runner often suffers a sharp pain in the side, but here the phrase names a simple sewing technique of in-and-out stitches

explanation.surface: What ails someone out on a run: a pain in the side.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points at a stitch, the side pain runners get; the answer is a basic sewing stitch made by running the needle in and out.
explanation.definitionFit: A sewing term for even in-and-out needlework, punning on the side pain a runner gets.

clue.text: All the same a corporate image is required

explanation.surface: Everyone must look alike when a company insists on a house style.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means unvarying, identical throughout; as a noun it is the outfit staff wear to present one company look.

clue.text: Man may be one and fifty

indicators.note: the letters of the word one may be rearranged into another order here

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A man could be counted as one, or as fifty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man may be one' reads as a riddle about counting; 'Man' is the definition and 'may be' the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A male first name, so a particular man could bear it.

clue.text: Having no spare key is of little importance

parts.note: taken as written
spare can mean lean or slight, as in a spare frame
G is a musical key

explanation.surface: Not having a spare key hardly matters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spare' looks like 'extra', but it means lean, slender.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as in 'it's a mere trifle, it's nothing', a thing that hardly counts.

clue.text: Relatively superior women in hospital

parts.note: female siblings are relatives, and the same title is given to senior nurses, who outrank others on a hospital ward

explanation.surface: Women in a hospital who hold rather senior posts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relatively' hints at family relations; in British hospitals a senior nurse in charge of a ward is called a Sister.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both female siblings, who are relatives, and senior nurses ranking above others on a ward.

clue.text: This is about the pupil making a bloomer

explanation.surface: A schoolchild makes a howler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pupil' and 'bloomer' suggest a student's mistake; really they are the centre of the eye and a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: The coloured ring of the eye surrounds the pupil, and the same word names a garden flower, something that blooms.

clue.text: Collaborate to swindle? Sure thing!

parts.note: a con is a swindle or trick
a cert is short for certainty, a sure thing, especially in betting

explanation.surface: Working together to cheat someone? Absolutely!
explanation.definitionFit: To act in concert is to work jointly, so as a verb it means cooperate.

clue.text: A professional looking down in the mouth

definitions.text: A professional looking down in the mouth

parts.words: A professional looking down in the mouth
parts.note: down in the mouth usually means glum, but here it is literal: a specialist peering down into a patient's mouth

explanation.surface: A gloomy-faced professional person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down in the mouth' is an idiom for sad; read literally it describes someone peering into a patient's mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: A tooth specialist who operates inside the mouth, literally looking down into it.

clue.text: The rat refused to act as a cleaner

indicators.note: to act as something is to play a role, so the letters here take on a new shape

explanation.surface: A rodent declined to work as a cleaner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'act' signals the anagram of all thirteen letters of THE RAT REFUSED.
explanation.definitionFit: A cleaning tool of plumes on a stick for whisking away dust.

clue.text: Getting some of them in entails standing out

indicators.note: only part of the phrase them in entails is used, the run inside it

explanation.surface: Getting some of them included means sticking out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some of' marks the letters running across 'them in entails'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone notable or prominent is conspicuous, rising above others.

clue.text: Go in maybe and look around, being smart

indicators.note: the word for look sits around the rearranged letters

parts.note: to see is to look

indicators.note: maybe signals the letters of Go in may be put another way

explanation.surface: Perhaps go in and have a look round, being clever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go in maybe' reads as an invitation; 'maybe' is the anagram signal, and 'around' tells you the look word wraps the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes someone well groomed and elegant, from French, so neat and well turned out.

clue.text: Assumed to approve

parts.note: taken as written
to OK something is to approve it

explanation.surface: Presumed it was meant for agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: Took on, as in assumed a role or took on a duty, past tense.

clue.text: Played dumb

parts.note: usually means pretended ignorance, but here means acted without speaking

explanation.surface: Pretended not to know.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Played dumb' is an idiom for feigning ignorance; literally, it means performed in silence.
explanation.definitionFit: Acted out without words, as in charades, so performed silently.

clue.text: Made some advance for a time before Easter

explanation.surface: Gave a loan for a period before the spring festival.
explanation.definitionFit: Past tense of giving a loan, an advance of money; also the Christian forty-day season of fasting preceding the spring festival.

clue.text: Foreign currency in hand-in a reserve fund

indicators.note: in signals the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Foreign money in your hand, handed in to a reserve fund.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' marks the run across 'hand-in a reserve'.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of money used in Serbia and several Arab countries.

clue.text: Getting a flat done up can be ruinous!

indicators.note: a flat done up is refurbished, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Renovating an apartment can wreck you!
explanation.walkthrough: 'done up' signals the anagram of A FLAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Disastrous or deadly, causing ruin.

clue.text: The troublesome child tucked into fish, which is staggering

indicators.note: one word is placed inside the other, as food is tucked into

parts.note: ling is a long sea fish like cod
an imp is a mischievous child

explanation.surface: The naughty kid scoffed fish, which is amazing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucked into' suggests the child is eating; it is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Walking unevenly, lurching, so lame and halting.

clue.text: Decide about a place in Washington

indicators.note: the word for decide goes about the letter a

parts.note: to settle a matter is to decide it

explanation.surface: Make up your mind about a spot in the US capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Washington here is the US state, not the capital.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest city of the north-western US state.

clue.text: Discharges a French lad — so wrong

parts.note: un is French for a

indicators.note: wrong signals that the letters of lad and so are set out incorrectly

explanation.surface: Fires a young French boy, which is unjust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' turns LAD SO into LOADS.
explanation.definitionFit: Empties out a cargo or load, so offloads.

clue.text: Clothes for the young still in recent fashion

indicators.note: one word is set inside the other

parts.note: late means recent, in the fashion of lately
yet means still, as in not yet done

explanation.surface: Baby clothes are still in the latest style.
explanation.definitionFit: A complete set of garments and linen prepared for a newborn baby.

clue.text: Turn corrupt and make something on the side

parts.note: to spin is to turn
food that has gone off is rotten, corrupt

explanation.surface: Go bad and earn a little extra money.
explanation.definitionFit: A by-product or secondary venture coming out of a main one.

clue.text: Spoke tartly and split

explanation.surface: Answered sharply and stormed off.
explanation.definitionFit: Barked out angrily, and also broke in two with a crack.

clue.text: Fish raised by a retired person

explanation.surface: A fish brought up by a pensioner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' means gone to bed, not stopped working.
explanation.definitionFit: A goby-like fish family is so called; and someone who has retired for the night is slumbering.

clue.text: Board assisting elderly

explanation.surface: A committee helping old people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Board' looks like a committee; it means bed and meals, as in a French boarding house.
explanation.definitionFit: In French usage it is a boarding house with meals; it is also a regular retirement payment supporting old people.

clue.text: The painter made to leave always returned

parts.note: to go is to leave

indicators.note: the word for always is read back to front

parts.note: ay is an old poetic word for always

explanation.surface: The artist forced out keeps coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' reverses AY to YA.
explanation.definitionFit: Francisco de Goya, the Spanish court artist.

clue.text: His constructive work is the tops!

definitions.text: His constructive work is the tops!

parts.words: His constructive work is the tops!
parts.note: the tops sounds like praise, but literally means the tops of houses, the roofs this tradesman covers

explanation.surface: A builder whose work is excellent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the tops' sounds like praise; literally it is roofs, which this tradesman covers.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradesman who lays slates or ceramic pieces on roofs and walls.

clue.text: A Greek character cutting extra large burden

indicators.note: the Greek letter cuts into the size abbreviation

parts.note: OS is outsize, an extra large clothing size
nu is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A Greek person slicing a huge weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting' suggests slicing; it is the container signal. 'Extra large' is the clothing-size abbreviation outsize.
explanation.definitionFit: A responsibility or obligation, as in the burden of proof.

clue.text: Appear pleased if the drink's about right

indicators.note: the drink goes about the letter for right

parts.note: gin is a drink

explanation.surface: Look happy if the drink is just right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts GIN round R.
explanation.definitionFit: To smile broadly, showing you are happy.

clue.text: The charge made for a certain plant

explanation.surface: The fee paid for a particular plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charge' looks like a fee; it means a sudden dash at the enemy.
explanation.definitionFit: A headlong dash or attack, and a marsh plant with hollow stems.

clue.text: Not perhaps a S American city's province

indicators.note: perhaps signals that the letters of not may be shuffled

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a South American city

explanation.surface: Not, perhaps, a Brazilian city's region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' turns NOT into ONT.
explanation.definitionFit: The Canadian region containing Toronto and Ottawa.

clue.text: A woman long holding gold pound

indicators.note: the word for long holds the other letters inside

parts.note: to pine is to long for
Au is the chemical symbol for gold
L is for libra, the pound

explanation.surface: A lady yearning for a gold sovereign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pound' is the weight or money abbreviation from Latin libra; 'holding' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's first name, so a particular woman.

clue.text: At one time coppers could get simple transport

definitions.text: At one time coppers could get simple transport

parts.words: At one time coppers could get simple transport
parts.note: coppers suggests police, but means copper coins, two old British coins that name an early bicycle

explanation.surface: Police officers used to ride basic vehicles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coppers' suggests police; it means copper coins. The penny and the farthing were old British coins, and a bicycle with one big and one small wheel was named after them.
explanation.definitionFit: A Victorian bicycle with a huge front wheel and tiny rear one, named after two coins.
